context: Wire each measurement into the path that would actually consult it, and make the packet-facing ones visible in the scored report rather than only on demand. Prefer surfacing over blocking: these are diagnostics and freshness signals, and turning a heuristic into a categorical gate failure is the defect this effort has repeatedly hit. Fix the mtime and empty-report holes with content hashing and an explicit unguarded-report case.
description: The 2026-08-03 batch added four integrity measurements and left all four as library functions no automated path calls, verified by inspecting the CLI entrypoints: identity_drift (cross-generation environment drift) is absent from behavioral audit main; class_coverage and candidate_staleness are absent from the Codex audit CLI; and the per-run prose_verification_conflict diagnostic is emitted on every scored run but never aggregated or surfaced in the report. A measurement nothing runs is a measurement that silently rots, and the facts they expose are exactly the ones a promotion packet must not omit - the v5 candidate being stale against 49 changed live files, and 5 of 6 gate-exercised record classes being absent from the artifact under promotion. Two smaller defects from the same batch belong here: candidate_staleness compares mtimes, so touching a file without changing content reports false staleness; and _refuse_clobber returns without guarding when the existing report has no scores key or an empty one, leaving a report that was once written empty permanently unprotected.

preserves.behavior: Committed evidence, isolation manifests, and scored reports keep their values
Diagnostics stay diagnostics; no text heuristic becomes a categorical gate failure
Live Codex and Claude memory and settings remain byte-unchanged
